doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Becoming Chick's engineer and moving to California
summary: Next albums My Spanish Heart and Music Magic, becoming Chick's concert mixer in 1977, and working as an independent.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Luckily it was mono. So you apparently passed Chick’s audition with “Leprechaun.” Did he officially in some fashion say you’re going to be my guy?

No not really. I mean we did that recording and then he called me up for the next project basically, which was “My Spanish Heart” which was the next album, and went out to Los Angeles to do that. And it was just taking it a day at a time with that and what I was doing was still in New York working. And then I got the idea — oh on the next project we did, we did the last “Return to Forever” album called “Music Magic” out in Colorado. And it was just after that I thought you know what? I think I’m going to move to — well no I went on the road with him at that point. I became his concert sound mixer at that point, after that project. That was in ’77. And it was that experience, getting to know everybody, all the people around him and so forth, touring, as you know, creates a special bond, a camaraderie. And I decided to move to California. And then I was just still working project to project. I really was kind of quote a staff member just for a very short period of time, not much at all. Basically I was an independent guy all these years, associated strongly but not necessarily a salaried person.
How do you charge for your expertise? Is there a recording engineer’s union?
No I think you find out what people are getting and see if you can too. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
